title: What's this?
goal: Name the things around you, make them plural, and ask questions with ten question words — while seeing that Pashto plurals also follow the gender you met in the last unit.
bekal: name things in the house and in your room
make plurals of both masculine and feminine words
ask questions with څه، څوک، چېرته، کله، ولې، څنګه، څو، کوم

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — په کوټه کې
dialogs.intro: Zarghuna takes Budi to his room upstairs. Budi points at things one by one, and Zarghuna patiently names them.

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: دا ستاسو کوټه ده. راځئ، دننه شئ.
lines.baca: dā stāso koṭa da. rādzəy, dənəna shəy.
lines.id: This is your room. Please come in.
lines.literal: this of-you(pl) room is. come-you(pl), inside become-you(pl).

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Thank you very much. What's this?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: دا مېز دی، او دا څوکۍ ده.
lines.baca: dā mez day, aw dā tsokəy da.
lines.id: This is a table, and this is a chair.
lines.literal: this table is, and this chair is.

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: هغه کتابونه دي. زما د ورور کتابونه دي.
lines.baca: hagha kitābūna dī. zmā də wror kitābūna dī.
lines.id: Those are books. My brother's books.
lines.literal: those books are. of-me of brother books are.

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: کړکۍ هلته ده. له هغې څخه غرونه ښکاري.
lines.baca: kṛkəy halta da. lə haghe tsəkha gharūna ṣkārī.
lines.id: The window is over there. You can see the mountains from it.
lines.literal: window there is. from that from mountains seen-are.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: ډېر ښکلي غرونه! هغه کوم غر دی؟
lines.baca: ḍer ṣkulī gharūna! hagha kūm ghar day?
lines.id: Beautiful mountains! Which mountain is that?
lines.literal: very beautiful mountains! that which mountain is?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: هغه د پغمان غر دی. په ژمي کې تل واوره لري.
lines.baca: hagha də Paghmān ghar day. pə zhamī ke təl wāwra larī.
lines.id: That's the Paghman mountain. There's always snow on it in winter.
lines.literal: that of Paghman mountain is. in winter in always snow has-it.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Why are there so many flowers here?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: ځکه چې زما مور ګلان خوښوي. دا زمونږ باغ دی.
lines.baca: dzəka che zmā mor gulān khwaṣawī. dā zmūẓ bāgh day.
lines.id: Because my mother loves flowers. This is our garden.
lines.literal: because that of-me mother flowers likes-she. this of-us garden is.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: When do you pick the flowers?

lines.speaker: زرغونه:
lines.text: په پسرلي کې. اوس آرام وکړئ، ډوډۍ چمتو ده.
lines.baca: pə psarlī ke. os ārām wəkṛəy, ḍoḍəy chamto da.
lines.id: In spring. Now get some rest — the food is ready.
lines.literal: in spring in. now rest do-you(pl), food ready is.

notes: Notice the pair دا and هغه throughout the dialogue. The word دا means "this" for something close, هغه means "that" for something far away — and هغه is the same word as "he/she". Pashto does not tell them apart; context takes care of it.

The verb "to be" in the plural is always دي, whether masculine or feminine. This is the one place where gender takes a rest: کتابونه دي (they are books) and څوکۍ دي (they are chairs) use exactly the same form.

To negate, just put نه right before the verb. Zarghuna says زه **نه** پوهېږم — "I don't understand". The word نه never moves anywhere else and is never split; it sticks to the front of its verb like a shadow.

The phrase نه پوهېږم is the sentence that will save you most often in Afghanistan. Literally "I don't understand", and much more polite than silence. Its partner: بیا ووایئ *byā wowāyəy*, "please say it again".
The word ځکه چې means "because", and it always comes as a pair — ځکه alone means "therefore", چې alone means "that". Together they make one conjunction you will use every day.

The sentence واوره لري literally means "snow has-it". Pashto uses the verb "to have" for things English says with "there is": the mountain "has snow", rather than "there is snow on the mountain". The verb لرل is covered fully in the next unit.

grammars.title: Plurals: four patterns that cover almost everything
body: Pashto plurals depend on gender and the ending of the word, just like the adjectives in the last unit. The first four rows of the table below cover most everyday words.
One relief: Pashto **does not use the full plural after numbers**. For "three books" it uses the counting form درې کتابه, not درې کتابونه. The numbers section at the back of the book deals with it.

grammars.title: Ten question words, and where they go in the sentence
body: Pashto does not rearrange the sentence to ask a question. The question word stands exactly where the answer will later stand, and the rest stays like an ordinary sentence with the verb at the end.
Compare these two lines: تاسو **کابل** ته ځئ (you are going to Kabul) and تاسو **چېرته** ځئ؟ (where are you going?). Only one word changes; the order stays intact.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Three words whose form is misleading
items: The word اوبه *ūba* means "water", and its form is **always plural**. So the sentence is اوبه سړې **دي** (the water is cold) with plural دي, not ده. English treats water as one thing; Pashto treats it as many.
The word ډوډۍ *ḍoḍəy* means both "bread" and "food" in general. The invitation to eat is ډوډۍ وخورئ, literally "eat bread" — even when what is served is Kabuli rice and meat.

The word ور *war* means "door", and it sounds almost the same as ورور *wror* (brother). The difference is just one syllable, and Afghans will know at once which you mean from the sentence. Still, say both aloud now.

blocks.title: Lifesaving phrases for your first week
items: The phrase دا څه دی؟ *dā tsə day* — "what's this?". On its own this sentence can teach you a hundred words a day, as long as you dare to point.
The phrase دا په پښتو څه وایي؟ *dā pə paṣto tsə wāyī* — "what is this called in Pashto?". A little longer, far more useful.
The phrase زه نه پوهېږم *zə nə poheẓəm* — "I don't understand". Don't be shy about using it; people will repeat more slowly, not give up.
The phrase ورو ووایئ *wro wowāyəy* — "please speak slowly". This is what keeps your conversation alive when the other person gets excited.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the right question word.
Put the words in the right order.

answers: دا څه دی؟ — کړکۍ چېرته ده؟ — هغه کتابونه دي. — زه نه پوهېږم. — څو کوټې دي؟
دا څه دی؟ — هغه کتابونه دي. — کړکۍ چېرته ده؟ — زه نه پوهېږم. — دا زمونږ باغ دی.
wave: Walk around your own room, point, and say دا څه دی؟, then answer yourself. Ten things, three minutes — and tomorrow do it again without looking at the list.
